name: Virgen
kurzbeschreibung: Charming village in the Virgental valley, home to the renowned Pfarrkirche zum Heiligen Virgil – one of the most beautiful villages in Osttirol.
beschreibung:
Overview

Virgen is situated at an elevation of 1,194 meters in the sun-drenched Virgental valley in East Tyrol, cradled between the glaciated peaks of the Venediger Group to the north and the rugged Lasörling Group to the south. Located roughly seven kilometers west of Huben in the Iseltal valley, the municipal area encompasses historic hamlets including Obermauern, Mellitz, Mitteldorf, and Welzelach, home to approximately 2,230 residents. Celebrated as the 'Sun Village of Hohe Tauern National Park', Virgen enjoys an exceptionally mild, sunny microclimate on a broad alluvial fan with remarkable alpine flora. As a designated Austrian Mountaineering Village (Bergsteigerdorf), Virgen champions sustainable alpine tourism balanced with traditional mountain farming and world-class artistic heritage.

History

Inhabitation of the valley dates to the Bronze and Hallstatt eras, evidenced by the prehistoric cremation necropolis at Welzelach and the discovery of a bronze situla urn. The settlement was first documented between 1185 and 1189 in the annals of Admont Abbey through Sigemar of Virgen. During the Middle Ages, the territory was ruled by the Counts of Görz before passing to Emperor Maximilian I and Tyrol in 1500. Perched high above the valley on a rocky ridge stands Castle Rabenstein: covering 4,800 square meters, the 12th-century stronghold is the third-largest medieval fortress in Tyrol and served as the district judicial seat until 1703. A crowning cultural jewel is the pilgrimage Church of Maria Schnee in Obermauern: completed around 1456 in Late Gothic style, it houses an extraordinary fresco cycle painted in 1484 by Simon von Taisten illustrating the Passion of Christ. Following a plague vow made in 1635, the annual procession of the decorated Virgental sacrificial ram is recognized as intangible UNESCO Cultural Heritage. The Parish Church of Saints Virgil and Vigilius features a soaring 72-meter spire.

Getting There

By car, travel from the north via the Felbertauern Road B108 through the Felbertauern Tunnel to Matrei in Osttirol, turning at Huben onto state road L24 into the Virgental. From the south, take the B100 to Lienz and follow the B108 northward to Huben. Train travelers arrive at Lienz railway station along the Drau Valley line. From Lienz station forecourt, frequent VVT regional bus line 951 runs directly through Huben to Virgen and onward to Prägraten am Großvenediger.

Tips

A rewarding cultural walk follows the scenic wayside stations from Virgen up to the Church of Maria Schnee in Obermauern to view the Simon von Taisten Gothic frescoes. Families will enjoy the shaded forest educational trail climbing from Mellitz to the ruins of Castle Rabenstein, rewarding walkers with vistas across the valley. Mountain enthusiasts utilize Virgen as an access hub for the legendary Venediger High Trail or high-altitude hikes into the Lasörling Group toward the Lasörlinghütte refuge at 2,293 meters and Lake Berger See.
